corrections.caveats: The 40x figure is not a measurement. The llhttp side (~500ns) is a hand-estimated cost model in docs/archive/ALGORITHM_IMPORT_COMPLETE.md, and no llhttp benchmark exists in the repo (benchmarks/fasterapi/bench_http1_parser.cpp only times FasterAPI's own parser). The parser does not import llhttp's generated state tables. It is a hand-written parser of about 350 lines, described in the repo as 'llhttp concepts (simplified)'. The companion doc docs/archive/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md compares the same 12ns against an estimated '~800 ns' for FastAPI (Python) and calls it 66x. It gives only 'M2 MacBook Pro' as hardware, with no compiler or flags. The claimed 15ns for an 8-header POST (1.8ns per header) is implausibly fast for a byte-wise state machine, which suggests a benchmark artifact. Every doc carries the author's own banner: 'Research note — snapshot, not current state ... experimental testbed, not a framework.'

tier_reason: The README table matches the record exactly (133 vs 1,377, 161 vs 1,602 and 374 vs 2,021 ns/op; 0 vs 5,177-5,345 B/op; 495-641 vs 48-98 MB/s), measured against net/http.ReadRequest on an Apple M1 Pro. The benchmark code is public (parser/parser_test.go), but the Go toolchain version and flags are not stated, so it stays C.

corrections.caveats: The benchmark code (parser/parser_test.go) is public and the hardware (Apple M1 Pro) is stated. The Go toolchain version and flags are not stated; go.mod only has the 'go 1.24.1' language directive, so it is not Tier A. The comparison is not like-for-like. The net/http benchmarks create a new bufio.NewReader (4 KB buffer) on every iteration and build a full *http.Request, which accounts for much of the 5 KB/op, while this parser only records byte offsets. The README also lists missing features that net/http has: no chunked decoding, no request-smuggling (CL/TE conflict) checks, silent Content-Length overflow, no header size cap, no bare-LF or obs-fold handling, and requests only. net/http is not one of the named category baselines (llhttp, http-parser, picohttpparser), but it is the de facto Go incumbent. No license, 0 stars, a single commit.
